cues: The key is the number of alpha hydrogens, hydrogens on the carbon carrying the nitro group, because nitrous acid attacks there.
A primary nitroalkane has two: it forms a nitrolic acid, which gives a blood red colour with alkali.
A secondary has one: it forms a pseudonitrole, blue.
A tertiary has none: no reaction, colourless.
